member.name: T:MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.Functions.ExponentialIntegralFunction
member.summary: Represents the exponential integral function, defined as: E_1(x) = \int_x^\infty (e^(-t) / t) dt for x > 0. Evaluates the single analytical integral function without multiple summation terms.

remarks.para: Numerical Methods and Domain Partition (x <= 1.0 vs x > 1.0): The calculation employs two distinct analytical and numerical formulations partitioned at the optimal threshold x = 1.0 (Abramowitz & Stegun §5.1, Gautschi 1973):

item.description: E_1(x) = -\gamma - \ln(x) - \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{(-x)^k}{k \cdot k!}, where \gamma is the Euler-Mascheroni constant (). For x \in (0, 1], the factorial denominator ensures rapid super-exponential convergence to the requested tolerance in ~10-15 iterations, while explicitly capturing the logarithmic singularity -\ln(x) as x \to 0^+. Using this series for x >> 1 is numerically forbidden due to catastrophic cancellation: alternating terms become exceedingly large before decaying (e.g. |term| > 10^7 for x = 20), destroying all double-precision significant digits when subtracting large numbers to produce a tiny result.

E_1(x) = e^(-x) \cdot \cfrac{1}{x + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{x + \cfrac{2}{1 + \cfrac{2}{x + \dots}}}}} (Gautschi / Cephes algorithm). For x > 1.0, the continued fraction convergents converge monotonically and rapidly without subtraction of large numbers, completely avoiding catastrophic cancellation. The exponential damping factor e^(-x) is factored out and applied at the end. As x \to 0^+, the continued fraction converges very slowly and cannot handle the logarithmic singularity, making it unsuitable for small x.

remarks.para: Cutoff Threshold: For x > MaximumAcceptedVariableValue = -\ln(\text{Tolerance}), e^(-x) < \text{Tolerance}, allowing the function to immediately return 0.0 without numerical evaluation.

member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.Functions.ExponentialIntegralFunction.Calculate(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Calculates the definite exponential integral over the interval [, ]: \int_{lowerLimit}^{upperLimit} (e^(-t) / t) dt = E_1(lowerLimit) - E_1(upperLimit).
member.param: The lower integration limit (a >= 0).
The upper integration limit (b >= 0).
member.returns: The calculated definite integral value.

remarks.para: Exposing a 2-parameter definite integral method offers decisive numerical and computational advantages over evaluating separate single-variable calls:

list.item: Singularity & NaN Cancellation (lowerLimit, upperLimit \to 0): In physical viscoelastic models (such as Fung quasi-linear viscoelasticity), the relaxation integral evaluates limits of the form a = t / \tau_2 and b = t / \tau_1. When t \to 0^+, evaluating E_1(a) - E_1(b) individually produces \infty - \infty = \text{NaN}. This method resolves the singularity analytically: when both limits are below , \lim_{a,b \to 0^+} [E_1(a) - E_1(b)] = \ln(b / a).

Algebraic Constant Elimination (upperLimit <= 1.0): When both limits fall within the power series domain, the Euler-Mascheroni constant cancels analytically, and the logarithms combine into a single \ln(b / a), saving transcendental function evaluations and reducing rounding accumulation.
Early Short-Circuiting: Returns 0.0 immediately if equals (within ), or if >= , bypassing numerical iteration entirely.

member.summary: Computes the alternating power series summation: S(x) = \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{(-x)^k}{k \cdot k!}.

member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.Functions.ExponentialIntegralFunction.EvaluateContinuedFraction(System.Double)
member.summary: Evaluates the exponential integral E_1(x) for x > 1.0 via the Gautschi / Cephes continued fraction: E_1(x) = e^(-x) \cdot \cfrac{1}{x + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{x + \cfrac{2}{1 + \cfrac{2}{x + \dots}}}}}.
member.param: The argument x > 1.0.
member.returns: The evaluated value E_1(x).
member.remarks:
Evaluated via the three-term Euler-Wallis forward recurrence:
For odd step index k = 3, 5, \dots: a_k = 1 + \frac{k - 1}{2}, \quad b_k = 1.0.
For even step index k = 2, 4, \dots: a_k = \frac{k}{2}, \quad b_k = x.
p_k = b_k \cdot p_{k-1} + a_k \cdot p_{k-2}, with p_0 = 1, p_1 = 1.
q_k = b_k \cdot q_{k-1} + a_k \cdot q_{k-2}, with q_0 = x, q_1 = x + 1.
Convergent ratio: r_k = \frac{p_k}{q_k}. If |p_k| > \text{RescalingThreshold} = 2^{57}, all recurrence terms are divided by \text{RescalingThreshold} to prevent IEEE 754 overflow.
Iteration terminates when the relative change satisfies \left|\frac{r_k - r_{k-1}}{r_k}\right| < \text{tolerance}, returning r_k \cdot e^(-x).

member.name: M:MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.NumericalMethods.DifferentialEquation.IDifferentialEquationMethod.Calculate(MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.NumericalMethods.NumericalMethodInput,System.Double,MelloSilveiraTools.Mathematics.NumericalMethods.NumericalMethodOutput)
member.summary: Advances the dynamic system by one time step, computing the state (displacement, velocity, acceleration and equivalent force) at the requested instant .
member.param: The system data: time step Δt (s), mass matrix [M] (kg), stiffness matrix [K] (N/m), damping matrix [C] (N·s/m), the equivalent force vector at (N) and the number of boundary conditions. Δt is read from input.TimeStep and must be consistent across calls so that the integration constants remain valid.
The current instant, in seconds, at which the output must be evaluated. Must be greater than or equal to the configured initial time.
The state at the previous instant time − Δt. Must not be for any step beyond the initial one. At the initial instant the implementation returns the initial state directly and ignores this argument.
member.returns: The numerical state of the system at .
member.remarks: Implementations integrate a second-order ODE of the form [M]ẍ + [C]ẋ + [K]x = F(t). The classic uses γ = 1/2, β = 1/4 (constant-average-acceleration) which is unconditionally stable and second-order accurate. The variant uses γ = 1/2, β = 1/6 (linear-acceleration), which is conditionally stable (Δt must be small relative to the highest natural period) but provides better phase accuracy.
